newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK's NFC sells BRS car leasing to GE.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK's NFC sells BRS car leasing to GE.

text.p: Freight transport firm NFC Plc launched a fresh round of restructuring on Wednesday, selling a clutch of non-core businesses, including its British BRS Car Lease business to U.S. firm GE Capital for 120 million pounds in cash.
It also completed the sale of its Lynx express parcels service in Britain to local management for 26 million pounds, including 23 million in cash.
The company announced the moves with its half-year results. Pretax profits rose 12.9 percent to 50.1 million pounds for the six months to March 31, on flat turnover of just over 1.17 billion pounds.
The interim dividend was maintained at 2.5 pence a share on earnings up 0.4 pence at 4.3 pence.

But the company warned that the overhaul would hit this year's full year results with an exceptional charge of 49 million pounds, offset by an exceptional profit of 20 million pounds from the disposals.
The share price was up 1-1/2 pence on the news at 129-1/2p by 1300 GMT.
NFC said it had also sold removals division Pickfords' businesses in the U.S. and Canada to Australian group Brambles Industries.
Together the BRS, Lynx and Brambles deals were expected to yield net cash proceeds of 145 million pounds in the current year and an exceptional profit of 20 million pounds.
And the rationalisation was expected to bring in a further 62 million pounds from surplus asset sales and withdrawal from three loss-making contracts in Britain.
But NFC said it would also be spending 39 million pounds of cash on restructuring work.
The company said it was reorganising the BRS truck rental and contract hire and engineering business and has closed its Exel Logistics Next Day Pallet network.

It said it was also consolidating its European management structure and undertaking a major overhaul of the loss-making continental European logistics business, with more cost cutting, disposals and closures planned.
"We have now freed up significant capital and management capacity for investment in our more attractive growth markets," chief executive Dr Gerry Murphy said.
